title: Conjunctive coNP reductions to sparse targets in Lean
claims: A pinned polynomial-time conjunctive reduction from a coNP-hard language to a sparse target suffices for P = NP, without a fixed query count.
A measured query-history frontier machine preserves existential correctness or certifies a positive result using cumulative sparsity.
A fixed-width conjunctive reduction of a pinned NP-hard or coNP-hard language to a cumulatively sparse target implies P = NP.
Sparse coNP-hardness implies P = NP using a measured dual frontier pruning machine.
An exact-length polynomially sparse coNP-hard target exists exactly when P = NP.
A polynomial-time selector for a pinned NP-hard target suffices for P = NP and its existence is equivalent to the pinned equality.
An input-supplied unary count gives a reference polynomial-time machine that returns the first accepting witness in exactly the given short-word-first prefix.
Every reference NP language admits complete witness recovery in polynomial time in its input and sufficient explicit unary padding.
A cumulatively polynomially sparse NP-hard target implies P = NP under the pinned definitions.
The existence of an exact-length polynomially sparse NP-hard target is equivalent to P = NP.
The pinned machine model supports polynomial-time lookup of any specified reduction image in an encoded candidate list.
Sparse pruning of encoded candidate frontiers is realized by a pinned polynomial-time machine with the cap supplied in unary.
A polynomial-time encoded child generator lifts to a polynomial-time flat map on encoded candidate frontiers.
For any pinned NP source and NP-hard target, a pinned polynomial-time map sends pairs into the target exactly when either component is in the source.
The finite list algorithm preserves existential membership while bounding the frontier under cumulative sparsity.
If NP is contained in P, any pinned normal-form verifier admits a polynomial-time witness producer with explicit failure.
The existence of polynomial-time witness producers for all pinned normal-form verifiers is equivalent to P = NP.
A polynomial enumeration budget covering an accepted witness for each yes-input suffices for polynomial-time witness production.
A pinned polynomial-time decoder with a logarithmic seed covering an accepted witness for each yes-input suffices for polynomial-time decision.

An arbitrary pinned polynomial-time verifier can be searched through a polynomial-size prefix of the reference Boolean-word enumeration. If the prefix contains a witness for every yes-input, the corresponding language belongs to P.
Languages with a polynomial-time verifier and a logarithmic-length certificate for each yes-input belong to P.
The exact P subset NP inclusion follows from pinned reference L010.

experiments.purpose: Run the pinned exact-statement checker when the reference checkout is available and otherwise report unavailability.
